description: Focus-dependent historical benchmarks for game years 1200-1800 (about AD 360 to 1360: the late imperial age, the successor kingdoms and the high agrarian expansion). A society that pours itself into one research line or a mixed archetype is judged against what comparable societies achieved with that emphasis: higher bands on its focus metrics, lower bands elsewhere, and at least one required cost below the base typical. Human summary and calibration notes: docs/research/BENCHMARKS_FOCUS_1800.md. Resolver and validator: tools/research/focus_bench.py.

position_scale.meaning: a band position on the base band's own scale, oriented so larger is better ('neither' metrics: numerically larger)

anchors.-2: worse plausibility bound (min; max for 'lower' metrics)
anchors.2: better plausibility bound (max; min for 'lower' metrics)

position_scale.interpolation: linear between anchors, geometric for metrics listed as 'log' in metric_scales; positions interpolate linearly between years
position_scale.modifier: [low_pos, typical_pos, high_pos]; min and max never move; an omitted metric is neutral [-1, 0, 1]
position_scale.construction: from each focus metric's signed design strength s (x era_weight): boost -> [-1 + 0.15 s, 0.5 s, min(1 + 0.25 s, 1.5)]; cost a = |s| -> [-1 - 0.15 a, -0.4 a, 1 - 0.35 a]. Shifted ('neither') metrics use the same formulas with up = +. Year 1200 is the join: focus_bench.py judges year 1200 with the 600-1200 file, so this file's 1200 row copies that file's 1200 positions (neutral where it has none; era-weighted profile for the five archetypes new in this window) and the band is continuous; this window's profile takes over by 1300. Metrics marked carried_from_1200 are 600-1200 effects that fade to neutral by 1300. Required costs therefore apply from 1300.

era_weight_doc: Line focuses, balanced and the five generic archetypes apply at full strength throughout. The four 600-1200 era archetypes continue with weights that follow their historical analogues: palace courts and temple estates fade slowly, citizen militias revive with the communes after 1500, steppe-edge powers stay strong, and territorial empires peak around 1400 and again with the great steppe conquest around 1700. The five new era archetypes grow in: feudal-manorial realms and examination empires mature by 1500-1600, merchant republics by 1600, scholastic-clerical realms by 1600, and nomadic empires peak around 1700. The 1200 key of every continuing focus is the 600-1200 file's.

roles.boost: focus metric: effective typical above the base typical; may pass the effective high by allowed_lead.per_metric (else .boosted) x |high - typical|
roles.cost: effective typical below the base typical; no lead past the (lowered) high
roles.shift: 'neither' metric moved up or down (e.g. more people under arms); must stay inside the shifted low..high
roles.context: largest_settlement_historical and major_innovations_per_century describe the whole era's record, not the player's society; this window's profiles never modify them

shock_hazard_mult_doc: Per focus, optional multipliers on benchmarks_1800.json shock_widening.hazard_per_game_century: merchant republics, trade leagues and empires suffer more pandemics and credit panics, nomadic empires more wars and succession collapses, examination empires more invasions, stewards and examination empires fewer famines, feudal realms more private war and peasant risings.

classification.rule: share = emphasis units on a line / all units (the research_emphasis order). 1) An archetype matches when its lines hold >= 55% combined, >= 12% each, and no line holds >= 40%; the best combined share wins. 2) Otherwise every line with share >= 25% gets weight min(1, (share - 1/12) / (0.40 - 1/12)); any remaining weight goes to 'balanced'; weights are normalised and the focus is that blend. 3) Nothing >= 25%: balanced. A line focus's labor/decree 'signature' adds 0.15 to its line's share. Timed strategies are classified per phase. Same thresholds as the 0-600 file.

surrogate_proxies._doc: Metrics without a probe_key have no absolute surrogate measure; these facets stand in for them in the relative (same-seed balanced) checks.
defense_labor_share: defense_share (surrogate row field, not yet a facet)
